_comment: Registry of the point clouds behind the hosted surveys (tools/lidar/points_publish.py).
points/<survey>/index.json            the survey's revisions, and index.html for people
points/<survey>/<rev>/tiles.geojson   one feature per tile: footprint, url, bytes, points, md5
points/<survey>/<rev>/urls.txt        every tile URL, one a line (wget -i / aria2c -i)
<survey> is the id of the survey in datasets.json.
REVISIONS. r0 is the cloud as the surveyor delivered it. Where a public agency already
serves r0 well it is NOT copied here: 'hosted': false and 'upstream' names where to get it.
r1, r2 ... are ours. A revision is never overwritten or deleted once published: a re-run
is a new revision whose 'parent' names what it was made from, and a DEM in datasets.json
names the revision it was gridded from ('products' here). Two kinds:
'full'    every tile rewritten (a re-classification); the tiles are hosted.
'recipe'  few points change (a constant shift, moved casts, a rule set applied on read);
the revision is a small corrections file plus the parent, no second copy.
Not used yet; the topobathy stream will be the first to emit one.
Gated surveys never get an entry: this bucket is public.

surveys.title: Kenai Peninsula 2008 lidar
surveys.citation: NOAA National Geodetic Survey, Remote Sensing Division: Integrated Ocean and Coastal Mapping (IOCM) lidar, Kenai Peninsula, 2008 (Aero-Metric); distributed by USGS 3DEP as AK_Kenai_2008. Public domain.

revisions.label: As delivered
revisions.notes: Not mirrored here: USGS serves it from a public bucket. Flown 2008-05-21 to 09-22, about 1.2 points per square metre, heights in metres NAVD88.

revisions.label: Ground re-classified (progressive TIN densification)
revisions.format: LAZ (LAS 1.2, point format 1), 2 km tiles named by their south-west corner
revisions.vertical_datum: NAVD88, metres (as delivered; not declared in the tile headers)
changes: Read from r0's octree and reprojected from EPSG:3857 to EPSG:6334.
Points the surveyor classed as noise (7 and 10) were dropped.

The classification of every point was replaced: 2 where Axelsson progressive TIN densification (angle 40, distance 3, seed 10 m, outlier detection off) took the point as ground, 1 otherwise. The surveyor's classes are not kept; they are in r0.
Every other attribute is as delivered.

Cut into 2 km tiles. Each tile was classified with a 30 m margin of its neighbours' points, then cropped to its own square. A point lying exactly on a shared edge is in both tiles, which is why this revision has 140,921 more points than r0 in total, net of the noise points dropped.
Stray returns far above and below the ground were not removed (outlier detection off); they are class 1.
revisions.why: No public bare-earth surface exists for this survey, and the surveyor's ground class lost 20.5% of crest cells on a hand-scored test patch against the 2019 Homer survey, where this classification lost 11.9%.
